body: You know the size, so you should probably resize, and grab the ptr to do direct assignments. It would ensure only one allocation

there is no need to make this a `uint8_t` as your struct will be padded anyway. Using `uint32_t` will take exactly the same amount of space, will remove all the casts you have, and allow wider range on the costs.
You want to move that outside the loop, reserve the max Size (4 if no diagonals), and just call `nbors.clear()` here, to avoid all the allocations (except the first one).
you can remove this and reuse the previous one.
This value seems like an internal thing, only used during the function calculation. Maybe remove it and use an array you allocate only during the function.

Are you sure you need this ? Are you not guaranteed that flow_direction will be overriden in the next loops ? (And value should probably be a separate things, as I commented below). You iterate over all the points below, so just assign `= Vector2();` in your continue branch ?
`TypedArray` does not have `ptr` method, but I've added a resize...

Yeah, flow_directions needs to be cleared, otherwise inaccessible regions would still have directions from previous calculation.
Thanks, fixed, I need to remember that.

`result[index++] = _get_point_unchecked(x, y)->flow_direction;` 
Would even be better to have the raw pointer somehow, to avoid all the boundchecks for every access, but not sure it's doable in the current state
If you stored the Vector2 flow_direction in a parrallel array instead of directly in the point, then all of this can just become a `memcpy` which will be faster because it will be vectorized.

I think it would be good to have a version that could take a subset of the whole A star grid 
(`void AStarGrid2D::calculate_flow_field(const Vector2i &p_id, bool p_ignore_obstacles, Rect2i subregion)` ). I could definitely see a use case in games to have a huge AStarGrid for your level, but wanted to recalculate only subportions for it in some cases (like give me the flow field only 10 units around this unit). Maybe that could be in a follow up PR if the need arise. But the code would need to change just very little, only the indexes part will change and you'll need a distinction between width and pitch.
why not write `p.flow_direction = p.pos.direction_to(e->pos);` directly at this stage, this would remove the need for the `Calculate flow directions.` loop, no ?
I said you that it's not possible with TypedArray
The main point of this comment is to remove the superfluous `Vector2i` constructor call. The other part is just a comment on the API, you can just ignore it.
I think I've made it. Check again.
Done, also removed ignore_obstacles since the algorithm is changed and not the whole grid is scanned for directions...

I've simply removed that method - feel free to implement it yourself.

I don't know if clearing everything is better than just the region you were asked. Could see people being surprised by both. Maybe add somewhere in the documentation that even requesting a sub region invalidates the whole region ?
I would probably reserve around 16 slots  to avoid the (2 - 4 - 8) reallocations.
This is a little wasteful as the region_to_check may be a lot smaller. But you'll need to update the `_to_index` method if you change it.
I would suggest saving a previous region to a variable inside AStarGrid2D - then clear it only when the regions are equal.
Or provide a parameter like "clear_previous_regions".

I'd say `open_list` should be a priority queue to ensure proper iteration order (by non-descending cost). Otherwise the same point could be enlisted many times which theoretically should result in worse time complexity (probably needs benchmarking though :thinking:).

There's this max heap implementation:

Min heap would do here so the above could be used with different `LessThan` comparator (`Indexer` is not needed here though).
